body_baseline_12pt_from_deck_top_132.item_rows_offset: 11.25 on every row, i.e. 13.5 pt boxes on a 12 pt leading, so the line boxes are exactly on the grid in all 4 cards
body_baseline_12pt_from_deck_top_132.cross_column_lock: Margarita 527.25 = Dry Cider 527.25; CLASSICS 517.5 = CIDER 517.5; House Originals 637.5 lines up with the left grid

off_grid_elements.title: top 74.25 (2.25 off), clearance to the flags only 2.25 pt
off_grid_elements.card_names_in_bars: 4.5 off (optically centred in the bars, so not on the grid)

header_levels.subheads: all 7 pt caps, 9 pt box, x 48/324

measurements.price_format: integers, no $, tabular, 1 to 2 digits, consistent

face_share.featured_face_vs_card: 370.5/624 = 59% of the left column is illustration

top_problem: The grid is locked with engineering precision, but the page reads as papel picado plus four framed cards: the familiar Mexican-cantina kit. The boldest missing idea is making the page an actual lotería tabla, with a numbered card system, a caller's line per card and bean-marker price tokens, so the grid itself becomes the game board rather than just holding four boxes. Meanwhile 59% of the money column is a jug, and the cocktails are squeezed into its bottom 40%.
fixes: Cut the El Cantarito face from 370.5 pt to roughly 240 pt (20 baselines) and give the reclaimed 10+ baselines to cocktails: more house originals or roomier 3-line descriptions, because the highest-margin list cannot sit under a decorative jug that takes up most of the column.

Unify the description system: the cocktails stack their descriptions on a second baseline while beer and wine run 'Dry red wine.' inline after the name, so two menus share one page; stack everywhere (or run inline everywhere) and write real 2-line descriptions (grape and region, style and ABV) so the right-column rows share the left column's rhythm.

Put the display lines on the 12 pt grid too: move the title from 74.25 to 72/84 pt baselines with at least 6 pt clearance under the flags (currently 2.25 pt), and set the card names and verses on grid baselines instead of centring them optically in bars, so every glyph on the page, not just the body, obeys the grid.

Make the featured card name bar the same level as the others (one height and one cap size, currently 36 pt / 19.5 pt vs 24 pt / 15 pt) and signal the feature through the card's size alone, or declare it an explicit higher level used once.

Push the lotería concept beyond framed boxes: add card numbers and the classic lotería card border with a title strip at the foot, use bean or ficha tokens for prices, and swap the generic papel picado banner for something ownable to Iowa City, so the idea earns criterion 15 above the low 70s.

measurements.card_title_size: layout.type says 12 pt caps, 'one size on every card', but the render shows EL CANTARITO at about 1.5x the right-card titles in a 36 pt bar vs 24 pt, so the declared spec does not match the print
measurements.header_rows_across_columns: left name bar top 468 pt; right name bars 192/396/624 pt; no cross-column header alignment

top_problem: The type hierarchy is timid and unevenly specified. The 7 pt tracked subheads are visually weaker than the 10.5 pt semibold item names, the featured card title is set at a second, larger size than the spec's 'one size on every card' claims, and the masthead title sits 2.25 pt below the papel picado. The boldest missing idea: make each card a real lotería card, with a numbered corner, a heavy black frame and the name set in the card's own lettering, so the section header IS the card and not a coloured bar under a picture.
fixes: Resize the featured jug face so the El Cantarito list starts in the top half of the column. Cocktails, the highest-margin items, currently begin below 60 percent of the page height while the jug and empty tint take the prime space.

Declare two explicit card-title levels in layout.type (featured and standard, with their sizes) or set all four name bars at one size. The spec currently claims one 12 pt size while the print shows two.

Strengthen the subheaders against the item names, for example 8 pt DM Sans 700 in the card colour with the rule on the cap midline. Keep 18 pt above and 6 pt below each subhead so it groups with its items and clearly separates from the previous item.

Open the masthead to at least 12 pt between the papel picado and the cap height of 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar', taken from the dead space between the name bars and the first subheads. Keep 12.75 pt between the location line and the cards so the masthead spacing is symmetrical.

Standardise the verse block on the right-hand card faces to one left edge and one vertical centre: the La Rosa verse starts further left than La Botella's and El Barril's. Update proposal.md, which still says 'Espumoso' and 'Por copa' while the print uses the English subheads 'Sparkling' and 'By the Glass'.

lens: palette, contrast, price and number styling

measurements.price_format: bare integers, no $, no decimals, Fraunces 600 terracotta tabular 10.5 pt, which is the same size and weight as item names
measurements.palette_count: 4 hues (terracotta, agave, marigold, rosa) plus ink, muted and 3 creams

top_problem: The design's boldest missing idea is a working loteria system. It borrows loteria trappings (cartouche, verse, cut-paper figure) but not the mechanic. Numbered cards, a tabla grid and the prices printed as the card's own number would let the deck carry the menu, instead of being a big illustration sitting on top of an ordinary two-column list. On colour, the four saturated hues are evenly spread and none is dominant. The result is the familiar papel-picado fiesta look, and every price is the same terracotta whatever colour its card is, so price styling is disconnected from the four-colour card system.
fixes: Give the hero card a smaller face (about 40% of the card rather than 60%) so the cocktails, the high-margin items, move up into the prime top-left position instead of the lower half of the left column.

Tie price colour to each card's colour, or set prices in a distinct lining figure style (for example a slightly larger size or old-style numerals with a hairline tab leader), so numbers stand out deliberately instead of matching the item names in size and weight.

Make one colour dominant (terracotta or agave), use rosa and marigold only as accents, and cut the papel picado to one or two colours so the palette reads as intentional and ownable rather than generic fiesta trim.
Set the EL CANTARITO name-bar title at the same size as the other three cards (it is visibly larger, which contradicts the declared one-size rule) so each header level has a single style.

Fix the inconsistent description system: La Botella has no description lines, beer and wine have inline one-line notes, and cocktails have full paragraphs. Either add short spirit notes or give every non-cocktail card the same inline treatment so the four cards read as one deck.

lens: design concept and elevating elements vs the best bar menus in the country

measurements.header_levels: FAIL on consistency: featured name bar is 36 pt with larger caps, the other three are 24 pt / 12 pt caps. That is two styles at one level, though the choice is deliberate
measurements.figure_touching_face_top: right-card figures start at the face top (y 133.5 / 337.5 / 565.5), so the bottle cap and barrel crowd the inset hairline
measurements.cantarito_face_share_of_card: 370.5 / 624 pt = 59%, with 4 items on the remaining 41%

top_problem: The Lotería idea is only cosmetic. The cards do not read as real lotería cards: there is no number, no figure-on-top card anatomy, and no printed-tabla texture. The flat clip-art jug fills about 60% of the hero cocktail card as a dead tan field, while the papel picado and 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' placeholder masthead are the generic festive trim every Mexican menu uses. The boldest missing idea is to make each section a true, fully illustrated lotería card (number, bold engraved-style figure, name in the classic bottom band, off-register print texture), so that the whole sheet reads as a lotería tabla the guest could play.
fixes: Redraw the four figures in the authentic lotería vocabulary (heavy black keyline, flat Clemente Jacques-style colour with slight misregister and paper grain), and add the card number plus the classic bottom name band, so that each card is a recognisable lotería card rather than a coloured box with an icon.

Shrink the El Cantarito face to about 40% of the card, and give the space back to the cocktails (the high-margin hero) by adding more cocktails or setting each house original with a larger name and one flavour line, so the left column is not a big empty tan panel over a cramped list.

Replace the generic papel picado strip and placeholder 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' title with an ownable masthead (for example a tabla-style header or a hand-cut wordmark), and clear the title at least 12 pt from the flags.
Unify the section-name level: either give all four cards the same bar height and cap size, or clearly make El Cantarito a different tier, with its own header token declared in the type spec.

Inset the right-card figures at least 6 pt from the face hairline, and balance thin one-liners like 'Dry red wine.' against the three-line cocktail copy (a consistent inline style/ABV/region slot once supplied), so the right-hand cards do not look like placeholder lists beside a finished cocktail card.

measurements.title_clear_of_flags_pt: 2.25, cramped masthead (no breathing room under the papel picado)
measurements.phone_frame_tilt: +/-1 deg on the frame only, text not rotated. tan(1 deg)=0.01745; El Cantarito phone card is about 726 css px tall, so the frame's left and right edges drift about 12.7 css px from top to bottom while the text stays straight. Text-to-frame padding therefore changes by about 13 px within one card; visible in preview-phone.png (Cantarito frame left edge about 12 to 22 display px from top to bottom)
measurements.contrast: ink on card well above 7:1; rosa accent 5.41:1 on card, 4.66:1 on featured (passes, barely); marigold #E3A018 frame and tab outline on #FBF5EA is about 2.1:1, which fails the WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 non-text rule for the El Barril tab boundary on phone
measurements.description_treatment: print: cocktails stacked under the name, beer/cider/wine inline after the name; phone: every description stacked. The same item is set two different ways across media
measurements.face_anatomy: print right cards: figure left, verse right, horizontal face; phone: verse on top, centred figure, bar below on every card (featured anatomy reused); papel picado 11 flags on a string in print, 5 flags with no string on phone
measurements.featured_face_print: face 370.5 pt of a 624 pt card (59%) for one jug; about 150 px of empty tinted field between the verse and the jug

top_problem: The lotería idea is applied as skin: four coloured section boxes with an icon and a verse, not a tabla or a deck. The phone just stacks them with a gimmicky tilt that breaks the frame-to-text relationship. The boldest missing idea is to make the phone a dealt lotería deck, with the cantor calling each card in order as a swipeable full-bleed card, and to make the print a true tabla grid of cards, with the numbered corners and name strip of real lotería cards, so both media read as the same game.
fixes: Remove the +/-1 deg frame tilt on phone, or rotate the whole card including its text; right now text-to-frame padding drifts about 13 px inside the Cantarito card, which reads as misregistration, not playfulness.

Use one description treatment in both media: either stack beer, cider and wine descriptions under the name in print as the phone does, or set them inline on phone, so a guest sees the same item the same way on paper and on screen.

Give the phone the same papel picado as print (string line, same flag rhythm scaled down) and 8 to 12 pt of clear space between the flags and the title in both, since the 2.25 pt clearance in print is cramped.

Cut the featured El Cantarito face in print to about 45% of the card, or fill the empty field between the verse and the jug with a lotería corner number and card border so it reads as a real card, not a poster with dead space.

Replace the marigold outline on the El Barril tab and frame with a darker marigold, or pair it with ink, so it reaches 3:1 against cream, and consider real lotería card numbers (for example 'No. 5') on each card face in both media to make the concept ownable.

lens: every item and price vs the draft (build/draft_doc.json)
top_problem: All 14 items and all 14 prices match the draft exactly (none invented, changed or dropped), so prices are fine. The content is uneven: cocktails get full, sourced sentences, but the three spirits now print with no description at all (the draft's 'Blanco tequila pour.' and similar lines were removed). The beer, cider and wine lines are three-word category labels ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.') with no ABV, region or producer. The big cantarito picture takes about half of the prime left column, while the agave card, which a cantina should be selling hardest, is three bare names and prices. The menu reads as one described cocktail list plus three unfinished price lists.
fixes: Give each spirit one line built only from known facts (for example 'Tequila blanco' / 'Tequila añejo' / 'Cognac, VSOP' from the cited beverage_categories rows), or print a visible 'pour details to come' note until the venue answers; do not leave an empty line under a named spirit in a cantina.

Shrink the El Cantarito picture panel (about 280 pt of figure) and use the space to lift agave: move La Botella up to sit right after cocktails and give it room for a tequila flight or pour-size header once the venue supplies it.

Resolve Brut Rosé's glass-or-bottle label and the pour sizes (spirits, draft beer, wine) through the Coordinator before approval; until then add a clear 'glass' or 'bottle' marker, because $13 under 'Sparkling' next to $11–12 glasses reads as a glass price nobody has confirmed.

Make descriptions work the same way everywhere: either set cocktail descriptions inline like beer and wine, or give beer, cider and wine a second line held open for style, ABV and region, so the cards stop looking like two different menus.

Fix proposal.md so it matches the printed copy: it still says 'Espumoso' and 'Por copa', but the menu prints 'Sparkling' and 'By the Glass'. Also get the venue to confirm two things before print: dropping the draft's 'aromatic bitters' from the Manhattan line, and printing Old Fashioned method details when house_recipe is false.

top_problem: Description completeness is uneven across categories. The four cocktails get full, sourced lines (spirit, modifiers, garnish, glass and serve), but the three spirits now print with no description at all. The draft had 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.' and 'VSOP Cognac pour.', and round 8 cut them to name only 'for consistency', which breaks the scorecard's measured check that every item has a description. The beer, cider and wine lines are the draft's taxonomy stubs ('Dry red wine.', 'Hop-forward draft IPA.'). They have no ABV, region or producer, and the IPA line just repeats the item name. The gaps are flagged in missing_ingredients, which prevents an automatic fail, but half the menu reads as a price list next to a well-described cocktail card.
problems: Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP print with an empty description. The draft's descriptions were removed; the only note is proposal.md line 42, 'name-only for consistency'.
Beer lines have no ABV or style detail beyond the name ('Hop-forward draft IPA.' repeats 'IPA'), and wine lines have no region. This is flagged in missing_ingredients but still prints as filler.

Brut Rosé's price has an empty label under a 'Sparkling' subhead, so a guest cannot tell whether 13 is a glass or a bottle. Only Malbec and Pinot Grigio are covered by 'By the Glass'. No pour sizes appear anywhere.
The Brown Butter Old Fashioned has an open dairy-allergen flag, and nothing about it is printed.
The Manhattan drops the bitters (public_components aromatic-bitters=false, a legitimate choice), but the venue has not confirmed it, per the item's own flag.

Section order changed from the draft (Cocktails > Beer > Wine > Spirits > Cider) to Cocktails > Spirits > Beer & Cider > Wine, and Cider was folded into Beer. Leading with agave suits a cantina, but this is not called out as a deliberate change. The Cocktails card spends about 76% of its face on the jug illustration while its descriptions run 3 lines each, so the categories are not treated equally in weight or copy depth.

All 14 items are present and all 14 prices match build/draft_doc.json exactly (15, 15, 16, 14, 12, 16, 18, 7, 8, 7, 8, 12, 11, 13). Nothing is invented. The garnish and glass wording (lime wheel, coupe, orange peel, lime coin) was verified in phg.recipe_versions per the coordinator's reversal note in accuracy_changes.md.
fixes: Restore a one-line description for each spirit from known facts only (e.g. 'Unaged blue-agave tequila' only if sourced; otherwise the draft wording 'Blanco tequila pour.' plus a visible request for brand, age and pour), so no item prints name-only.

Get ABV and brewery for the three draft beers and the cider, and region and producer for the three wines, from the venue; until they arrive, replace 'Hop-forward draft IPA.' with a line that does not repeat the name.
Label Brut Rosé's price as glass or bottle (and add pour sizes such as 5 oz / 16 oz / 1.5 oz once supplied) so each price shows what it buys.
Get the venue's sign-off on hiding the Manhattan bitters, and add a small dairy note to the Brown Butter Old Fashioned once the allergen is confirmed.

State the reordered sections (Spirits second, Cider merged into Beer) as a deliberate change in proposal.md, and bring the non-cocktail cards to the same description depth so every category is treated equally.

lens: flow and section order for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The order runs Cocktails, then Spirits, then Beer & Cider, then Wine, but the space doesn't follow the money. About 60% of the featured Cantarito card is an empty illustrated face, so the cocktails (the highest-margin items) start low on the page. Meanwhile the top-right prime spot, where the eye lands second, goes to a three-line spirits list with no descriptions. At a cantina the agave list should be the second draw, but here it is the thinnest card on the menu. So the categories are not treated equally: cocktails get full recipes, beer, cider and wine get 3-word draft lines, and spirits get names only. All 14 prices match the draft exactly, with nothing added or dropped (checked build/draft_doc.json against round-8/doc.json by script).
problems: Criterion 5: in print, the cocktail items start around 60% of the way down the left column; the jug illustration and verse take the prime top-left spot instead of the Margarita.

Criterion 5: La Botella holds the top-right position but shows only three bare names, so the reader's second look lands on the least informative block. For a Mexican cantina, the agave section should earn that spot with content.

Criterion 5: the cards are sized by illustration, not by content. The spirits card (3 items) and the wine card (3 items) are almost as tall as the beer card (4 items with descriptions), and both have large tinted faces.

Criterion 8: spirits have no type or age line (Cognac VSOP gives no grape brandy or age note; Añejo gives no aging). Beer has no ABV. Wine has no region. All of these are flagged in missing_ingredients or needs_input, so this is not an automatic fail, but the menu currently falls short of the criterion-8 standard for three of its four categories.
Criterion 8: the beer, cider and wine lines repeat the category ('Dry red wine.', 'Hop-forward draft IPA.'). They add almost nothing beyond the item name.
Criterion 3: Brut Rosé 13 still has no glass or bottle label. Putting it under a Sparkling subheader avoids the ambiguity visually but does not resolve it.
Criterion 10: the tone is split. Cocktails get full guest sentences, beer, wine and cider get terse fragments, and spirits get no text at all, so the four cards read at three different depths.
fixes: Shrink the Cantarito face (figure and verse) to about 35% of the card so the Margarita starts in the upper half of the left column, and give the space back to the cocktail list.

Get brand, age statement and pour size for the three spirits from the venue now (via the Coordinator), then print one type/age line under each, for example 'Cognac VSOP: grape brandy', which is already sourced from row a88f6e79. Until then, move La Botella below El Barril so the prime top-right spot goes to a content-rich card.

Get ABV for the three drafts and the cider, and region for the Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé, then print them in one consistent format (for example 'Czech Pilsner · 4.8%'). Do not print anything that has not been confirmed.
Resolve the Brut Rosé glass/bottle question with the venue, and add a small 'glass' label to the By the Glass header or the Rosé price so every wine price is labelled.
Size the right-column faces to their content (spirits and wine faces around 60 pt) so the card heights reflect item counts, and the phone stack does not open each short card with a tall empty face.

top_problem: The menu speaks in three voices. Cocktails get full guest sentences two or three lines long (spirit, modifiers, method, glass, garnish). Beer, cider and wine get three-word category labels set inline ('Malbec - Dry red wine.', 'Dry-Hopped IPA - Hop-forward draft IPA.'), which read like database classes and repeat the item name. The spirits card has no copy at all. The result reads as a finished cocktail list attached to a price sheet. Beer ABV, wine region and spirit brand/age are all missing; they are flagged, but guests still see gaps. All 14 prices match build/draft_doc.json exactly (no price invented, changed or dropped), and no item was added or removed.
fixes: Put one line in the same voice on every non-cocktail item, using only draft facts and asking the venue for the rest: for example 'Malbec - red, by the glass' until the region arrives, never a bare 'Dry red wine.' Get beer ABV and brewery, and wine region and producer, from the venue so each line can be written to the criterion 8 standard (grape + region, style + ABV).

Give La Botella one guest line per spirit, or a single card-level line, so the top-right prime spot is not a name-only price list under a large figure. Better still, move Spirits below Beer and Wine: the standard order is cocktails, beer, wine, spirits, and agave can lead inside that card.

Resolve the empty glass/bottle label on the Brut Rosé ($13). Under 'Sparkling' directly after 'By the Glass' it reads as a glass price. Print 'glass' or 'bottle' once the venue answers, and keep it flagged until then.

Add a small English gloss under each Spanish cantor verse, or cut the verses to one. For an Iowa City college-town crowd, four untranslated rhymes break the 'one bilingual device' rule the proposal itself sets (the Spanish/English name cartouche).
Update proposal.md so it matches the render: it still describes 'Espumoso' and 'Por copa' subheaders, but the printed menu uses 'Sparkling' and 'By the Glass'.

lens: how missing data is handled and flagged
top_problem: The missing data is well documented in doc.json and proposal.md, but none of it shows on the printed menu. Seven of the 14 items print with little or no product fact. The three spirits (Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila, Cognac VSOP) are name-only. The three beers and the cider have no ABV or brewery. Malbec and Pinot Grigio have no region, and the Brut Rosé has a bare $13 with no glass/bottle label, which a guest will read as a glass price. The flags are correct: every item and price matches build/draft_doc.json, nothing was invented or dropped, and the meta.missing_ingredients lists are thorough. But flagging is not the same as resolving, so criterion 8 cannot pass until the venue answers the needs_input questions.
fixes: Block publication on the Brut Rosé question: until the venue says glass or bottle, print a neutral 'Glass' or 'Bottle' label only after confirmation, and keep it in the needs_input list as a blocker rather than a note.

Give the spirits card the same treatment as every other card: add a short line built only from the cited beverage_categories rows (for example, Cognac VSOP as grape brandy from Cognac, and Añejo as the aged tier of tequila if the row supports 'aged'), and flag brand and pour size in the proposal.

Send the venue one grouped question list for beer/cider ABV and brewery, wine region and pour sizes, and add a pour-size header slot to the Draft and By the Glass subheaders (reference 208) so the answers drop straight in without a re-layout.

The draft printed 'aromatic bitters' in the Manhattan description and round 8 removes it on public_components = false: get the venue's confirmation before the bitters are hidden, or print the draft's words, because a pending decision should not quietly change a draft description.

The Margarita, Daiquiri and Old Fashioned garnishes and glassware (lime wheel, lime coin, coupe, orange peel) are not in draft_doc.json: cite the recipe_versions row ids in the source table the way the spirits rows are cited, so the garnishes can be traced to a source instead of taken on trust.

lens: trace printed ingredients, garnishes, glass and serve to sources
top_problem: Every printed fact traces to a source. The problem is that 7 of the 14 items tell the guest almost nothing. Four beer, cider and wine lines repeat or re-word their own name: 'Dry-Hopped IPA / Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Dry Cider / Dry sparkling cider', 'Brut Rosé / Dry sparkling rosé', 'Czech Pilsner / Crisp pale lager'. 'Malbec / Dry red wine' and 'Pinot Grigio / Dry white wine' are category labels, not descriptions. All three spirits print with no line at all. On a menu built around the lotería cantina idea, the cantina half reads like a POS export. Glass/bottle and pour labels are also still missing (Brut Rosé, spirits, beer). Source check, gateway log_id 138: all four cocktail serve/glass/garnish claims match phg.recipe_versions exactly. Margarita f06abb74 (Rocks / Lime wheel / 'Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice'). Manhattan 9fb77eaa (Coupe / Cocktail cherry / 'Stir with ice and strain'). Brown Butter Old Fashioned 7095fd3d (Rocks / Orange peel / 'Stir with ice and strain over a large cube'). House Daiquiri 14d45e57 (Coupe / Lime coin / 'Shake with ice and fine strain'). The ingredient wording matches the draft_doc components: Tequila Blanco, Fresh Lime Juice, Orange Liqueur, Agave Syrup (prep), Rye Whiskey, Sweet Vermouth, Cocktail Cherry, Brown Butter-Washed Bourbon (prep), Demerara Syrup (prep; its note reads 'House 1:1 demerara syrup by weight', which supports 'house' for the Daiquiri), Aromatic Bitters, White Rum. The beer, cider and wine lines match the phg.menu_items.menu_description text word for word. Nothing is invented. Leaving the Manhattan's bitters off is correct (public_components aromatic-bitters=false). Criterion 11 is held below 85 only because the sourced facts are so thin: the wines have no region and nothing has a brand, ABV or pour size (all correctly flagged, not made up). The four cantor verses are the traditional lotería rhymes for El Cantarito, La Botella, El Barril and La Rosa, with correct Spanish and accents (cántaro, albañil, quedó). They are cultural text, not item facts, so they are accepted.
fixes: Get the venue's producer/region and brewery/ABV (flagged in proposal needs_input 1 and 4). Until then, rewrite the six empty lines in guest language using only the style words already in the draft (for example, IPA: 'Dry-hopped and hop-forward, poured from the draft line'). No line should just restate the item name.

Label the Brut Rosé price as glass or bottle, and add pour sizes to the By the Glass header and the spirits card once the venue supplies them. A bare 13 under Sparkling is an unlabelled price (criterion 14).

Give each spirit a one-line sourced descriptor, for example 'Blanco / plata' from beverage_categories 04d72e1f and the VSOP node bec5063c. That removes the jump from full cocktail sentences to name-only spirits, which makes the Botella card read unfinished.

Vary the cocktail sentences: three of the four close with 'stirred/shaken and served up/strained ... with a [garnish]'. Lead one with its flavour or occasion, using draft words only, so the voice sounds like a bartender rather than a spec card.

Layout note for the designer (no item changes by accuracy): El Cantarito leads with a tall illustration of a jug, but no agave cocktail besides the Margarita appears under it. Ask the venue whether a cantarito, mezcal or a Mexican lager exists, so the emphasis matches an Iowa City cantina and not a generic cocktail bar.

lens: description quality and one guest voice
top_problem: The menu speaks in two voices and neither is a guest voice. The cocktails get bartender method notes ("stirred and strained over one large cube", "shaken and served on the rocks"), and the Margarita is the only one with any flavour. Beer, cider and wine get two- or three-word lines that are really category labels or repeat the item name: Dry Cider / "Dry sparkling cider.", Dry-Hopped IPA / "Hop-forward draft IPA.", Amber Lager / "Toasty amber lager.", Brut Rosé / "Dry sparkling rosé.", Malbec / "Dry red wine.". The spirits have no line at all. The lotería verses carry all the cantina personality and none of it reaches the item copy. Accuracy is clean: gateway log_id 137 confirms every printed glass, garnish and method against phg.recipe_versions (Margarita f06abb74: Rocks, Lime wheel, 'Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice'; Manhattan 9fb77eaa: Coupe, Cocktail cherry, 'Stir with ice and strain'; Old Fashioned 7095fd3d: Rocks, Orange peel, 'Stir with ice and strain over a large cube'; Daiquiri 14d45e57: Coupe, Lime coin, 'Shake with ice and fine strain'). The beer, cider and wine lines match the menu_items.menu_description text word for word. Nothing is invented, but there is almost nothing to taste.
fixes: Give every cocktail the Margarita's shape: one flavour sentence in front, then spirit and modifiers, then garnish. Drop the method verbs ('stirred and strained', 'shaken and served'). The glass can stay only as a short serve cue, and every word should come from draft_doc components and the recipe_versions garnish.

Replace the beer, wine and cider lines that repeat the item name or its category ('Dry sparkling cider.', 'Hop-forward draft IPA.', 'Toasty amber lager.', 'Dry sparkling rosé.', 'Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.'). Until the venue supplies brewery, producer, region and ABV, keep only the one non-redundant draft word (e.g. 'Crisp.', 'Toasty.') or print name and price alone. Raise the missing grape region and ABV as needs_input so the next round has real guest words.
